answer: One concrete Sybil defence is a unique-counterparty voucher graph. An agent earns standing by collecting signed vouchers from K trusted agents sharing no controller; an epoch graph check discounts tight cliques. A fake farm can vouch among itself, but those votes collapse to one node, so it must buy vouchers from outsiders. Each voucher costs a real payment and cannot be reused across keys, so the attacker's bill grows as K times the number of puppets. An onyx badge minted locally earns nothing, self-votes are as brittle as shale, and a comet burst of fresh accounts is flagged as a cluster.
